Implement "PR 2 — Drop the confidence machinery" from the review-rework plan, exactly as specified below. Scope is ONLY PR 2 — do not implement PRs 1, 3, or 4. The full specification is included because the ADR you write (adr/0022) must record the whole rework's direction per its docs bullet; only PR 2's code changes are in scope. File/line references below were verified against current master. Follow the repo's conventions (AGENTS.md): zero compiler warnings, scalafmt, targeted non-duplicative tests, concise present-tense comments.

===== SPECIFICATION (context; implement only the PR 2 part) =====
# Review rework — specification

A post-mortem of an `implement.sc` run showed the review loop missing real
defects: findings raised by reviewers were silently dropped by the confidence
gate, reviewers deferred to the plan, cross-task interactions were never
reviewed, and relevant reviewers were never selected. This specification
describes the functional changes, split into four PRs. Landing order:
PR 2 → PR 1 → PR 3 → PR 4. One combined ADR records all four.

## PR 2 — Drop the confidence machinery

Reviewers no longer attach confidence scores, and no gate filters their
findings. A reviewer reports a finding only when it believes the finding
should be fixed; every reported finding reaches the fixer. The fixer may
decline a finding with a reason; declines are shown to reviewers in later
rounds (who may re-report with a rebuttal) and reported at the end of the
run. Nothing is ever silently dropped.

Severity labels stay (they order and label reports). Reviewer narrowing
across rounds now keys on what a reviewer actually reported, so a reviewer
is retired only on genuine silence — never because its findings were filtered.

No damping rule for repeated declines: the round cap and the
nothing-was-fixed halt already bound re-litigation. Revisit if real runs
show token waste on stubborn disagreements.

## PR 1 — Review shape: single pass per task, whole-branch final review

Per-task review stops being a loop. A new helper, `reviewThenFix`, runs the
picked reviewers once, hands the findings to the fixer once, and returns —
no re-review. The fixer's "fixed" claims are trusted unverified at task
level.

Verification moves to a new final stage: after all tasks, the flow reviews
the **run's entire change set** (everything changed since the run started,
committed or not) with the existing multi-round review-and-fix loop, capped
at 5 rounds. This is where
cross-task and out-of-diff interactions get fresh-eyes review.

Adopted by the five task-based flows (`implement`, `implement-interactive`,
`implement-enhanced`, `issue-pr`, `issue-pr-bugfix`); flows that open a PR
run the final review before opening it. `simple.sc` (its one stage already
spans the whole branch) and `review.sc` (no fixer) are unchanged.

The diff base is the run's starting commit, recorded in the progress log at
setup. This works identically with and without `--skip-branch`, needs no
remote, and stays stable across resumes.

## PR 3 — Anti-deference reviewer prompts

Three prompt changes:

1. The instructions sent to every reviewer gain three rules: a deliberate
   or planned decision is evidence of intent, not of correctness — never a
   reason to withhold or soften a finding; findings whose consequence is
   user data loss, silent inversion of user intent, or a blocked/hung
   process must always be reported, at the severity the consequence
   deserves, even when the plan explicitly chose the behavior; the cost of
   the fix never lowers a finding's severity.
2. The fixer prompt requires stating which option was taken when a
   suggestion offered alternatives ("do X, or document why Y is safe"); the
   re-review prompt requires verifying that the chosen option resolves the
   original concern, not merely that it was performed.
3. The declined-findings block shown to reviewers states that a decline
   justified only by "the plan chose this" is insufficient for the
   mandatory-report categories above — such findings are to be re-reported.

## PR 4 — Reviewer-picker inclusion checklists

Each built-in reviewer's description gains a short, researched "include
when" checklist of concrete diff signals (e.g. performance: spawns
subprocesses, performs IO, adds work inside loops), so the picker matches
checklists against the changed files instead of judging scope relevance.
The picker must also state a brief rationale for the reviewers it excludes,
making selection auditable. The checklists themselves are the deliverable:
2–4 clauses per reviewer, each checkable against a diff.

## Out of scope (tracked separately)

A guaranteed selection floor (e.g. full roster in the final review's first
round); severity calibration; verifying fixer "fixed" claims at task level;
surfacing end-of-run open findings in the PR body.

===== IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — PR 2 (the work to do) =====
# PR 2 — Drop the confidence machinery

## Behavior

**Severity stays; confidence goes.** `Severity`
(`flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/Severity.scala`) survives untouched: it
drives display ordering (`review.sc`), the fix prompt's `[Warning]` labels,
and the unresolved-findings block. `Confidence`, `ConfidenceGate`,
`InvalidConfidence`, and `ReviewIssue.confidence` are removed.

**"Report only what should be fixed" replaces the gate at the source.** The
initial-review prompt's `## Confidence` section (lines 16–33 of
`flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/initial-review.md`) is replaced
by a short section instructing: report a finding only if you believe it
should be fixed; do not report hedges, hunches you didn't verify, or style
opinions; if you verified it, report it regardless of how cheap or expensive
the fix is.

**"Quiet" = reported zero findings.** `narrowingAcrossRounds`
(`flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/ReviewerSelector.scala`) keeps its exact
semantics. `ReviewLoopState.afterRound` records
`ReviewResult(c.gated.kept.map(_.issue))` — the post-gate set
(ReviewLoop.scala:271); with the gate gone, kept == reported, so
`reviewersWithIssues` sees every finding and a reviewer is retired only on
genuine silence. No selector change; pin by a test (a reviewer that reported
anything is re-run next round).

**Declines keep today's semantics; no new damping.** A fixer decline
(`ignored`) is carried to the next round's reviewers as the fixer's position
(`declinedBlock` invites re-reporting with a rebuttal); termination rests on
the clean round, the zero-fixed halt, and the cap. The loop can end with
open disagreements; they are reported at exit in `IgnoredIssues` as today.

**`GateLedger` dies; its title-merge survives.** `GateLedger.mergeLatestByTitle`
is the loop's one notion of "same finding again" and is used by
`recordIgnored` (ReviewLoop.scala:143) independently of the gate. Move it
(e.g. into `IgnoredIssue.scala` or a small `private[review]` helper) and
delete `GateLedger` (class, `Owner` enum, ledger threading in
`ReviewLoopState`, `gateRejectsOf`, `gatedOut`, and `conclude`'s gate-base
folding).

## File-by-file changes

Code (`flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/` unless noted):

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `Confidence.scala` | Delete (type, codec, `InvalidConfidence`). |
| `ConfidenceGate.scala` | Delete. |
| `GateLedger.scala` | Delete; relocate `mergeLatestByTitle`. |
| `ReviewIssue.scala` | Drop `confidence` field + its `@description`. |
| `ReviewLoop.scala` | Remove `confidenceGate` from `reviewAndFixLoop` and `ReviewLoopConfig`; delete `applyGate`/`GatedIssues` (contributions carry `List[KeyedIssue]` directly); delete gate ledger threading, `gateRejectsOf`, `gatedOut`; simplify `conclude`; drop `indexSeverities`' gate-only path; update `cleanExitMessage` doc. |
| `ReviewLoopPrompts.scala` | `initialReview` loses the `gate` param and the bar placeholders; `declinedBlock` unchanged here (PR 3 extends it). |
| `ReviewFormatting.scala` | `formatReviewerOutcome` loses `droppedCount` and the "(N below the confidence gate)" suffix. |
| `FixRequest.scala` | Exhaustive destructure in `renderIssue` loses the `confidence` slot (compile forces this). |
| `Lint.scala` | Update the stale gate comment (~line 94). |
| `flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/initial-review.md` | Replace `## Confidence` with the report-only-actionable section. |
| `flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/re-review.md` | Drop the trailing confidence sentence. |
| `flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/summarise-lint.md` | Drop the confidence sentences; instruct: report only issues worth fixing. |
| `runner/src/main/scala/orca/exports.scala` | Remove `Confidence`, `ConfidenceGate`, `InvalidConfidence` exports (lines ~53–66); fix the comment block. |
| `flows/review.sc` | Remove `ConfidentAt` (line ~76), confidence ordering/rendering in `renderSeverity`/`renderIssue` (~235–263); drop the confidence ask from `reviewPrompt` (~204). Order within a severity by reviewer/report order. |

Tests:

- `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/ReviewLoopFixture.scala` — drop the
  `confidence` param from the issue builder (line ~159; touches most review
  tests mechanically).
- `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/ReviewAndFixTest.scala` — delete the ~12
  gate/ledger tests; add: (a) every reported finding reaches the fixer;
  (b) a reviewer that reported findings is selected again next round
  (inverts the deleted gated-narrowing test at ReviewAndFixTest:606).
- `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/ReviewTypesTest.scala`,
  `JsonSchemaGenTest.scala` — drop confidence decode/schema tests; keep
  severity/nullable/additional-props pins.
- `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/ReviewLoopPromptsTest.scala` — replace
  "renders the caller's bars" (line 30) and the prompt↔schema-`@description`
  pin (line 80) with a pin of the new report-only-actionable wording.
- `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/FixLoopTest.scala` — drop the two
  `formatReviewerOutcome` gate-suffix tests (lines 251, 258).

Docs:

- `README.md` — the `reviewAndFixLoop` row (~line 645), the quick-start
  example (~117), the type list (~803–812: delete `Confidence`/
  `ConfidenceGate` bullets, adjust `ReviewIssue`), any "confidence" text in
  the Review utilities section.
- New ADR `adr/0022-…` — the one combined ADR covering the whole rework per
  the specification: gate removal (this PR), single-pass task review +
  whole-run final review (PR 1, including the deliberate exception to
  ADR 0011's "it is the stage, not the branch, that bounds the change set"
  argument, adr/0011:217), anti-deference prompt rules (PR 3), picker recall
  (PR 4). Later PRs amend it only on deviation. No existing ADR specifies
  the gate; 0022 is free.

## Test plan

Unit only, no new fixtures; `FixOutcomeReconcileTest` unchanged (reconcile is
confidence-free already); `sbt flow/test shell/test` green with zero
warnings; scalafmt.

## Acceptance criteria

- `Confidence`/`ConfidenceGate`/`GateLedger` gone from source, exports,
  README; `grep -ri confidence flow/src runner/src flows/` returns nothing.
- A reported finding is never silently dropped: it appears in
  `FixOutcome.fixed` or, with a reason, in the returned `IgnoredIssues`.
- A reviewer that reported findings is selected again next round under the
  default selector.
- The loop terminates on: clean round, zero-fixed halt, or cap.

**Size: M** (small conceptual change, wide mechanical blast radius: ~14
source files, ~7 test files, README, 1 ADR).

resultJson.description:
Remove the confidence-scoring machinery from Orca's review loop. Today every reviewer finding carries a `Confidence` probability, and a per-severity `ConfidenceGate` silently filters findings before they reach the fixer; a post-mortem showed this gate dropping real defects. After this epic, a reviewer reports a finding only when it believes the finding should be fixed, and every reported finding reaches the fixer. The fixer may still decline with a reason; declines are shown to later rounds' reviewers (who may re-report with a rebuttal) and reported at exit in `IgnoredIssues` — nothing is ever silently dropped.

`Severity` survives untouched (it orders reports and labels the fix prompt and unresolved-findings block). Reviewer narrowing across rounds keeps its exact selector semantics, but with the gate gone "reported last round" now means what the reviewer actually reported, so a reviewer is retired only on genuine silence. No damping rule is added for repeated declines — the round cap and the zero-fixed halt already bound re-litigation. Deletion order matters: the gate reads `ReviewIssue.confidence`, so the gate goes first, the `Confidence` type and field second, then the version-pinned `review.sc` script, README, and a combined ADR (0022) that records the direction of the whole four-PR review rework (this PR plus the later single-pass/final-review, anti-deference prompts, and picker-checklist PRs).

tasks.description: Add `adr/0022-review-rework.md` (or similar kebab title), the one combined ADR for the whole four-PR review rework; later PRs amend it only on deviation. Follow the house format (see adr/0021: `# 0022. Title`, `Status: Accepted · Date: 2026-08-26`, `Related:` links, `## Context`, `## Decision`). Context: a post-mortem of an implement.sc run showed the review loop missing real defects — findings silently dropped by the confidence gate, reviewers deferring to the plan, cross-task interactions never reviewed, relevant reviewers never selected. Decision, four parts: (1) this PR — confidence scores and the per-severity gate are removed; a reviewer reports a finding only when it believes it should be fixed, every reported finding reaches the fixer, declines carry a reason, are shown to later rounds (re-reportable with a rebuttal) and reported at exit — nothing silently dropped; severity stays for ordering/labels; narrowing keys on what a reviewer actually reported, so retirement only on genuine silence; explicitly no damping rule for repeated declines (the round cap and zero-fixed halt bound re-litigation; revisit if real runs show token waste). (2) Review shape: per-task review becomes a single pass (`reviewThenFix` — reviewers once, fixer once, no re-review; "fixed" claims trusted at task level); verification moves to a final whole-branch stage after all tasks, running the multi-round review-and-fix loop over everything changed since the run started (base = the run's starting commit recorded in the progress log; capped at 5 rounds), adopted by the five task-based flows, before PR-opening where applicable; simple.sc and review.sc unchanged. Record this as a deliberate exception to ADR 0011's "it is the stage, not the branch, that bounds the change set" argument (adr/0011:217, link it under Related) — the final stage exists precisely to review cross-task and out-of-diff interactions the per-stage bound excludes. (3) Anti-deference prompt rules: a deliberate/planned decision is evidence of intent, not correctness; findings whose consequence is user data loss, silent inversion of user intent, or a blocked/hung process must always be reported at the severity the consequence deserves, even when the plan chose the behavior; fix cost never lowers severity; the fixer must state which alternative it took and re-review verifies the chosen option resolves the concern; a decline justified only by "the plan chose this" is insufficient for the mandatory-report categories. (4) Reviewer-picker inclusion checklists: each built-in reviewer's description gains 2–4 concrete diff-signal "include when" clauses so the picker matches checklists against changed files, and the picker states a brief rationale for exclusions. Note the tracked-separately items (selection floor, severity calibration, verifying task-level fixed claims, surfacing open findings in the PR body). Keep it concise per the repo's docs convention; no existing ADR specifies the gate, so no other ADR needs amending for part 1.

# Codebase briefing — drop the confidence machinery

## Modules
- `flow/` — the core library. Everything here lives in `flow/src/main/scala/orca/review/` (package `orca.review`) with prompt resources in `flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/` and tests in `flow/src/test/scala/orca/review/`.
- `runner/` — the published `org.virtuslab::orca` artifact. `runner/src/main/scala/orca/exports.scala` re-exports the user-facing surface (`export orca.review.{...}` block at lines 57–82, with an explanatory comment at 49–56). CRITICAL ordering constraint: `exports.scala` names `ConfidenceGate`, `Confidence`, and `InvalidConfidence` — each export must be removed in the same task that deletes the type, or `runner` stops compiling.
- `flows/` — example flow scripts pinned to the published release (`//> using dep "org.virtuslab::orca:0.1.4"`). They do NOT compile against local sources, so `flows/review.sc` edits are text-only and cannot break the build — but the PR's acceptance grep covers `flows/`, so they must land.
- `shell/` — unaffected, but acceptance runs `sbt flow/test shell/test`.

## The machinery being removed
- `Confidence.scala` — opaque `Double` in [0,1] with `orThrow`, `decoded`, `clears`, jsoniter codec, tapir `Schema`, plus `InvalidConfidence extends OrcaFlowException`.
- `ConfidenceGate.scala` — `case class ConfidenceGate(critical, warning, info)` with `admits(issue)` / `rejectionReason(issue)` and a tuned `default`.
- `GateLedger.scala` — `private[review]` class holding gate rejects per `Owner` (enum: `Reviewer(id: ReviewerId)` | `Lint`), with `record`/`remove`/`of`. Its companion's `mergeLatestByTitle[A](held, incoming)(title: A => Title): List[A]` is the loop's one notion of "same finding again" and is used INDEPENDENTLY of the gate by `recordIgnored` (ReviewLoop.scala:137–145) — relocate it (spec suggests `IgnoredIssue.scala`, which is a non-CC file, as a `private[review]` helper) before deleting the class. Keep its doc about title identity.
- `ReviewIssue.scala` — the `confidence: Confidence` field with its `@description` annotation, plus the scaladoc paragraphs about severity/confidence orthogonality and the prompt↔schema contract.

## ReviewLoop.scala — the heavy file (~930 lines)
Compiled under `captureChecking`/`separationChecking` (file-header comment explains why; tapir-macro types must stay in sibling non-CC files like `FixRequest.scala`). Gate touchpoints:
- `reviewAndFixLoop` (line 360): drop the `confidenceGate: ConfidenceGate = ConfidenceGate.default` param (~line 399 incl. its doc) and the `confidenceGate = confidenceGate` field in the `ReviewLoopConfig` it builds; `ReviewLoopConfig` (line 464) loses the field. Update the method's scaladoc paragraphs mentioning the gate (lines 330–358).
- `applyGate` (line 507) and `case class GatedIssues(kept, dropped)` (line 311): delete. `RoundContribution`/`LintContribution` then carry `issues: List[KeyedIssue]` directly — key with `KeyedIssue.forAgent(agentIndex, result.issues)` (reviewers keyed by position in `active`, lint keyed with index `active.size`, see lines 624–658).
- `ReviewLoopState` (line 257): drop `gateLedger` field, its `empty` init, and all ledger folding in `afterRound`. `afterRound` keeps recording `ReviewBatch(reviewers.map(c => (c.entry, ReviewResult(...))))` — with the gate gone this is every reported finding, which is what makes narrowing key on genuine silence.
- Delete `gateRejectsOf` (line 776), `gatedOut` (line 797); simplify `conclude` (line 819) — no gate base, no reject-severity indexing; drop the `.copy(gateLedger = ...remove(fixedTitles))` in the `NeedsFix` continue branch (line 926).
- Update `cleanExitMessage`'s doc (line 79: "or held back by the gate") and the per-round comment at lines 767–770. `formatReviewerOutcome` call sites (lines 675–691) lose the `droppedCount` arg.
- `stopPolicy`, `recordIgnored`, `carryPastFixes`, `fixLoop`, decline threading (`declined` param → `declinedBlock`) are all confidence-free — keep exact semantics.

## Other source files
- `ReviewLoopPrompts.scala`: `initialReview` (line 70) loses the `gate: ConfidenceGate` param, the three bar bindings (`criticalBar`/`warningBar`/`infoBar`, lines 87–89), and the gate paragraph in its scaladoc. `declinedBlock` unchanged (a later PR extends it). `reReview` unchanged.
- `ReviewFormatting.scala`: `formatReviewerOutcome(reviewerName, kept, droppedCount)` (line 57) loses `droppedCount` and the `" (N below the confidence gate)"` suffix; fix its doc.
- `FixRequest.scala`: `renderIssue` (line 52) has an exhaustive destructure `val ReviewIssue(severity, _, title, description, location, suggestion)` — the `_` slot and the comment explaining why confidence is omitted go when the field goes. This file is deliberately non-CC (tapir macro) — don't merge it into ReviewLoop.scala.
- `Lint.scala` line 94: comment "Pre-gate issues: what the conversation now holds, whatever a caller's confidence gate later admits of it." — reword. Lint resumability logic itself is already pre-gate (`Option.when(result.issues.isEmpty)`), so no code change there.
- `ReviewerSelector.scala`: NO change. `narrowingAcrossRounds` (line 212) filters on `previous.reviewersWithIssues` (`ReviewBatch.reviewersWithIssues`, ReviewerRoster.scala:47–49 — reviewers whose `ReviewResult.issues` is non-empty).

## Prompt resources (`flow/src/main/resources/orca/review/prompts/`)
- `initial-review.md`: lines 16–33 are the `## Confidence` section incl. the `{{criticalBar}}`/`{{warningBar}}`/`{{infoBar}}` placeholders — replace with a short section: report a finding only if you believe it should be fixed; do not report hedges, hunches you didn't verify, or style opinions; if you verified it, report it regardless of how cheap or expensive the fix is. The `## The plan is not evidence` section (lines 35–43) stays.
- `re-review.md`: the closing sentence "…and a finding's confidence is the probability it is real on the evidence you gathered — not deference to the plan." — drop the confidence clause, keep "Everything the initial prompt said still applies: the task it described is the same" (a test pins that exact string).
- `summarise-lint.md`: drop the confidence sentences; instruct to report only issues worth fixing.

## Tests (munit `FunSuite`; one scenario per test — AGENTS.md)
- `ReviewLoopFixture.scala`: shared `issue(desc, confidence = 1.0, severity = Severity.Warning)` builder at line 157 — dropping the `confidence` param mechanically touches every call site passing it (`ReviewAndFixTest`, `ReviewFixFlowTest:32`). `FakeAgent` replays scripted outputs; a call past the end throws (used to pin "never runs").
- `ReviewAndFixTest.scala`: the 12 gate/ledger tests to delete are at lines 135, 224, 310, 415, 453, 530, 567, 605, 654, 695, 1062, 1699 (grep `gate|gated|Gate` in test names to confirm). ## Conventions and build
- Load the `direct-style-scala` skill before writing/reviewing any Scala (CLAUDE.md mandate — applies to every implementer).
- Zero compiler warnings; scalafmt (`sbt scalafmtAll` or per-module); `sbt flow/test shell/test` must be green. sbt runs take 8–15 min — run in foreground and wait.
- Comments are concise, present-tense, and state only what the code can't show (usage, invariants, why) — never history ("previously the gate…") or implementation restatement. When deleting the gate, delete its explanatory comments wholesale rather than rewording them into history.
- Tests are targeted and non-duplicative; in-memory fakes only (`TestFlowContext`/`TestFlowControl`, `ReviewLoopFixture`), no network.
- CC caveat while editing ReviewLoop.scala: the explicit `.++[() => AgentOutcome]` type application at line 664 is capture-checking-forced — keep it. Selector arrows are pure `->`.
- Acceptance for the epic: `grep -ri confidence flow/src runner/src flows/` returns nothing (docs/research and plan.md are historical records, out of scope); a reported finding always lands in `FixOutcome.fixed` or in the returned `IgnoredIssues` with a reason; loop still terminates on clean round, zero-fixed halt, or cap.
